title: Why women are often better investors than men
description:
Investing used to be seen as something that was for older people in suits, but now more young people are getting into it, thanks to the rise in online investing apps that have made it more accessible, and a growing awareness of how stocks and shares work.

But data suggests that despite being less likely to start investing, women often make higher returns than men when they do. So, why are women often better at investing? And how does it work?

BBC business reporter Emer Moreau unpacks the data on how women and men invest differently, what investing is and why it can be risky. We also chat to Viktoriia and Gabriella, two women in their 20s, about why they started investing and how they are finding it.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討女性在投資領域表現往往優於男性的原因，以及年輕女性參與股票與指數股票型基金 ETF 投資的經驗。節目中，BBC 商業記者 Emer Moreau 指出，雖然女性開始投資的比例較低，但因傾向採取長期持有、降低風險、減少頻繁交易與注重情緒管理等策略，往往能獲得更佳的長期報酬。受訪者 Viktoriia 與 Gabriella 分享了她們透過社群媒體啟蒙、運用 ETF 分散風險並克服短期波動的親身歷程。最後，個人理財專家 Mary 建議新手在投資前應做好自主研究、了解指數基金等工具，並根據個人財務目標進行風險控管。
summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, host Iqra Farooq and BBC business reporter Emer Moreau explore why women often achieve better long-term investment returns than men despite lower participation rates. Research indicates that women tend to be more risk-averse, trade less frequently, maintain emotional discipline, and favor diversified funds like ETFs rather than chasing short-term speculative gains. Young investors Viktoriia and Gabriella share their personal journeys of starting out via social media, overcoming early losses, and focusing on long-term compound growth. Personal finance expert Mary also offers key advice, emphasizing due diligence, low-cost index funds, and goal-oriented planning while remaining mindful of market risks.

And now three years later, I'm up by about £21,000, which is incredible because of consistency.

So, it's basically a less, well I don't want to say less risky because there is still risk involved, but it's a way of diversifying your money across loads of different individual stocks instead of just betting all your money on one stock, um, which can obviously be a lot more risky.
As I say, women tend to be more risk averse.
Women also tend to gravitate more towards what's called ESG investing, so that stands for environmental, social, and governance.

There was one study in India, so basically the the amount of money that's put in savings accounts in India is quite high, and that's basically attributed to the fact that women tend to put their money in savings accounts as opposed to investing.
